text: I was hurt in a car accident in Perth. Which compensation lawyers should I contact?

result.keyword: I was hurt in a car accident in Perth. Which compensation lawyers should I contact?
result.markdown:
I’m sorry you’ve been hurt. For a **car-accident injury in Perth**, I’d shortlist these firms for initial consultations. In WA, motor-injury claims generally run through the Insurance Commission of Western Australia (ICWA), and a lawyer can be particularly useful if liability, the extent of your injuries, or the amount of compensation is disputed. [www.icwa.wa.gov.au](https://www.icwa.wa.gov.au/motor-injury-insurance/make-an-injury-claim/compensation/do-i-need-a-lawyer?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Firms I’d contact

1. **Stephen Browne Lawyers** — **my first choice to speak to**
   - Perth personal-injury specialist with a dedicated motor-vehicle accident team.
   - Handles car, motorcycle, truck, pedestrian and catastrophic-injury claims.
   - Offers an obligation-free initial consultation and generally **No Win No Fee** for motor-vehicle claims.
   - Perth office: Level 6, 524 Hay St; (08) 9474 5244. Their team includes lawyers whose practice is specifically focused on motor-vehicle accident claims. [www.stephenbrowne.com.au](https://www.stephenbrowne.com.au/service/motor-vehicle-accident?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - [Stephen Browne – car accident claims](https://www.stephenbrowne.com.au/service/motor-vehicle-accident/car-accident-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

2. **LHD Lawyers Perth**
   - Strong option if you want a specialist compensation firm and **No Win No Fee** arrangement.
   - Their Perth team specifically handles ICWA motor-injury claims, treatment/income support and damages.
   - They list Abbey Tempest as a Perth senior associate whose career has predominantly focused on motor-vehicle accident claims. [www.lhd.com.au](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/wa/perth/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - [LHD Lawyers – Perth car accident claims](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/wa/perth/car-accident/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

3. **Slater and Gordon Lawyers Perth**
   - A larger national firm with a dedicated Perth car-accident team.
   - Offers No Win No Fee and handles CTP claims involving medical expenses, lost income and other compensation.
   - Their Perth lawyer Damon Marsh has practised exclusively in personal injury since 2017, including motor-vehicle accidents and complex/catastrophic injury matters. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/motor-vehicle-accidents/car-accident-lawyers-in-perth?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - [Slater and Gordon – Perth car accident lawyers](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/motor-vehicle-accidents/car-accident-lawyers-in-perth?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

4. **Separovic Injury Lawyers** — another Perth personal-injury specialist worth getting a competing opinion from.

### What I'd do

I'd **speak to Stephen Browne and LHD first**, then compare their advice and proposed costs before signing anything. You don't necessarily have to hire a lawyer: ICWA says most claims can be made directly, but you can appoint a lawyer at any stage. [www.icwa.wa.gov.au](https://www.icwa.wa.gov.au/motor-injury-insurance/make-an-injury-claim/compensation/do-i-need-a-lawyer?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Importantly, **don't choose solely on “No Win No Fee.”** Ask each firm:
- What exactly counts as a “win”?
- What happens to medical-report, barrister and other disbursement costs if you lose?
- Will there be any gap between costs recovered from ICWA and what you owe the firm?
- Who specifically will handle your file?
- What compensation categories do they think you may be entitled to?

ICWA specifically warns that No Win No Fee agreements can still leave you liable for disbursements or other costs, and that you should understand the costs agreement before proceeding. [www.icwa.wa.gov.au](https://www.icwa.wa.gov.au/motor-injury-insurance/make-an-injury-claim/compensation/do-i-need-a-lawyer?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**One important point:** WA generally has a **three-year limitation period for motor-vehicle claims**, but particular circumstances can create different requirements, so don't wait unnecessarily. [www.lhd.com.au](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/wa/perth/car-accident/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me **(1) roughly when the crash happened, (2) whether you were the driver/passenger/pedestrian, (3) whether the other driver was at fault, and (4) what injuries you suffered**, I can narrow this to the **2–3 lawyers I'd recommend most strongly for your particular situation**.
